chapter: Teaching, the 1951 Big Show and New York nights
title: Students sent by Barney Kessel and others; teaching as the future
summary: Most of his students come by reference from guitarists such as Barney Kessel, and he expects eventually to concentrate on passing on what he knows.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Are most of your students interested in jazz guitar?

Yes, I have a lot of students who are rock and roll players, very good players, you know. They're interested in jazz. But I get most of my students from performing, and by reference. And I say half of my students come from Mundell Lowe, Herb Ellis, Barney. I get all of Barney Barnie's students because Barney Barnie's never in town. You know. Speaking of the guy in Montana, Barney performed there and the guy was -- loved Barney's playing and he wanted to study with Barney Barnie and Barney gave him my number, and I'm getting this call from Jeff Foote or someone in Montana and I'm wondering who in the hell is this. And finally after about nine calls we got together and he told me, well I want to study with you because Barney highly recommended you. So he came here and stayed for two weeks this time. We studied, and I gave him material.
Then he'd come back for two more weeks, but this is how I get most of my students, from guitarists.
Barney Kessel, yes. Well you know,
Yes, Barney Kessel, yes, yes. Thank you. But any way, this is how I get most of my students. And
this is part of -- I will eventually wind up just teaching. You know, because this I thoroughly enjoy, and it keeps me mentally alert --
Do you want to play concerts or 0--

I say eventually, eventually this -- oh, I will always do a little performing, but I mean eventually I'm sure this is the direction I will take. Just -- because I've got to pass some of this on, you know, and as I say, I enjoy it and I enjoy seeing my students do something, accomplish something, you know. So I'm sure this is the direction I'll take.
But teachers are born. You know this.
